title: General chemistry II
purpose: Apply colligative properties, kinetics and mechanisms, equilibrium, acids, bases and buffers, titrations, solubility, entropy and free energy, electrochemistry, nuclear chemistry and metals in biology.

weeks.12: Coordination chemistry and metals in biology

blocks.deliverable: Find a rate law and a half-life from data.
Compute an equilibrium constant and predict shifts.
Compute the pH of the bicarbonate buffer at different ratios.
Week 7 midterm; read a titration curve and its equivalence point.
Relate ΔG, K and cell potential.
Compute a radioactive dose remaining and explain iron binding in hemoglobin.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Blood buffer model: use the bicarbonate system and the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation to predict pH changes, and compare them with clinical acid–base patterns.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
